messages:
harper: hit an onboarding oddity in the Go generator sampleapp: when the HTTP client drops the connection the handler returns but the generator keeps streaming and the SDK goroutine hangs. repro attached. seems like a mismatch between desired semantics (stop on client disconnect) and a couple of SDK internals that either ignore parent ctx or assume a detached background refresh.

harper: minimal handler:
```go
func Handler(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
  it := sdk.Generator("lumen").Stream(r.Context(), Prompt{Text: "draft"})
  for it.Next() {
    if _, err := w.Write([]byte(it.Text())); err != nil {
      log.Println("write failed", err)
      return
    }
  }
  if err := it.Err(); err != nil {
    log.Println("iter err", err)
  }
}
```

joel: thanks for the repro. two likely culprits: 1) auth/token refresher and transport reconnects use context.Background() so they outlive the request; 2) iterator doesn't expose a user-facing cancel/close so handlers can't cleanly tear down without cancelling the whole req ctx.

mica: one design nuance we discussed earlier: some callers actually want the generator to continue running even after the HTTP client disconnects (e.g., long-running background summarization kicked off by a web request). forcing a strict close on req cancel would prevent that. we should support both flows explicitly.

harper: agree. proposal: add two orthogonal primitives on the iterator: Close(ctx) for the common case (stop now, unblock Next, cleanup) and Detach() which makes the iterator intentionally independent of the request context so background work continues. default behavior remains tied to the parent's ctx unless Detach() is called.

joel: API sketch:
```go
type GenIter interface {
  Next() bool
  Text() string
  Err() error
  Close(ctx context.Context) error   // synchronous teardown, idempotent
  Detach()                          // makes iterator use a detached internal ctx and keep running after req cancel
}
```
Detach() should be safe to call only before the request finishes; its semantics: replace internal parent ctx with a background context and return immediately. Close(ctx) still works for detached iterators to stop them later.

mica: implementation notes: 1) threadable parent ctx: change refresher/reconnect to take a parent ctx and default to req ctx; 2) Detach() atomically swaps that parent to a background ctx; 3) ensure metrics/emitted logs note detached lifecycle so ops can find orphan streams. add a new field in observability to mark "detached: true" for these streams.

joel: also add README cookbook: patterns for web handlers: a) default (stop on client disconnect): create iterator with r.Context() and call Close on write error; b) background work: call it.Detach() then return 202/Location and optionally persist iterator id to monitor later. we need to add server-side cleanup for detached iterators (TTL or manual Close).

harper: good point about lifecycle. propose a small manager in SDK: DetachedTracker that tracks detached iterators with weak refs and TTL (default 24h) and exposes an admin endpoint to list/close them. that'll help ops and avoid silent leaked workloads.

mica: docs-bot: please add two cookbooks to Go SDK README (Stop-on-disconnect, Background-detach pattern) and a note in sampleapps demonstrating Detach() with a follow-up status endpoint. also grep repo for Context.Background() in auth/refresh code paths and prefer parent ctx injection.

docs-bot: action created: docs/issue-512 - add detach cookbook, update sampleapps.

joel: tests: unit to ensure Close unblocks Next when blocked on transport read; unit to ensure Detach switches to background ctx and iterator continues after parent ctx cancel; integration: simulate auth refresh and ensure parent ctx passed to refresh unless Detach() was called.

harper: i'll open a draft PR with the API, sampleapp changes, unit tests, and a simple DetachedTracker implementation (configurable TTL + admin list endpoint). tagging @mica @joel for review. thanks! :rocket:
